name: Tieree
body:
The tieree are intelligent oozes capable of maintaining a humanoid form and absorbing equipment to use or wear. Like the hedoro, tierees have origins related to humans and their like.

Unlike the hedoro, they are not themselves former humans, but aberrations. They have always been oozes, granted sapience by an unknown event around the same time that chemical slimes became publicly known.

Physical Description: Tierees have a physiology akin to gelatinous oozes and the various jellies that adventurers deal with on their quests. What sets them apart is their natural shape is roughly humanoid, allowing them to hide their true ancestry from others. When they’re not covering themselves, tierees can be of several different heritages, which can change their base size, the color of their body, and the viscosity and acidity of their ooze.

Base Height	Base Weight	Weight Modifier	Modifier
4 ft. 0 in.	162 lbs.	2d4	x5
Adult	Middle Age	Old	Venerable	Maximum Age
40	125	188	250	+2d% years

Society: Tierees have created an amalgam of other societies to use as their own; the end result of which is surprisingly human in function. They seek areas that are hospitable to them to live, take over if necessary, and transform them into regions from which they hope to one day expand. This is met with varying degrees of success depending on who’s on the other side of these pushes for expansion.

Relations: Tierees don’t care to deal with others physically unless they absolutely must. It is considered impolite in tieree culture to comment on one’s oozy exterior, and outright rude or fight-worthy to touch somebody without their express permission, which is reserved only for the closest of relatives or loved ones. Interestingly, unlike other oozes who divide to reproduce, tierees gather one or more partners who fuse consciousnesses into a new being with only the vaguest memories of their past, like remembering a relative you spent a week with as a child. A tieree without partners eventually discorporates and reforms as two or three oozes that may or may not still have sentience.

Alignment and Religion: Tierees are a dominating people, but not overtly evil. They have stringent rules about physical exertion and contact, and they maintain their status quo by falling in line with the societies in which they find themselves while traveling and adventuring. Tieree society has no recognizable pantheon of its own, but individuals may find reason to worship in their own right. Many turn to druidism to learn more about the natural world, its creatures, and its livery.

Adventurers: Young tieree treat it as a game to see how long it takes for their true selves to be found out by those with whom they associate. Once they’re discovered, however, most are quick to adapt and try to prove themselves useful as allies during an adventure. Their fluid forms allow tierees to function best as monks and rogues, but alchemists, druids, sorcerers, and the occasional wizard are not unheard of.

Tieree Names: Tierees have names that are easy to reproduce as an ooze comprised of pops, whistles, and fluttering noises.

Example Names: Datatat, Pfft, Swoooiiiizzs, Tadtadtadt, Thhhsshhh

Ancestry Traits

All tierees share the following traits.

Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Dexterity, +2 Intelligence, –4 Strength. Tierees are agile and very smart, but their uncovered form has great difficulty grabbing and holding onto things with any power.
Size: Medium. As Medium creatures, tierees have no special bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Speed: Slow. Tierees have a base speed of 20 feet, and their speed is never modified by armor or encumbrance.
Tremorsense: When touching a surface, tierees can pinpoint the space of other creatures within 60 feet that are also touching that surface. This doesn’t allow them to ignore the miss chance if they can’t otherwise see the creature, such as if it’s invisible or has total cover or concealment.
Type: Aberration. Tierees are aberrations, which grants them darkvision out to 60 ft.
Coating: A tieree in its natural form can coat an object or creature in ooze for up to 1 round per level. This requires a standard action for objects its size or creatures at least one size smaller than the tieree, and a full-round action for creatures or objects up to one size category larger. Double the amount of rounds required for each size larger a creature or object is than this limit. A creature coated in ooze that moves treats the first 10-feet of space each round as covered in grease, as the spell. This otherwise functions as a non-magical grease spell with a saving throw DC of 10 + 1/2 the tieree’s character level + its Constitution modifier. The tieree treats its character level as its caster level.
Incorporation: As a full-round action, a tieree in its natural form can engulf an unattended object a creature of its size could wear or wield, then project that object outward. This allows the tieree to wear or wield objects using its normal carrying capacity. When a tieree incorporates a full suit of clothing or armor, its form is considered solid until it removes them and it can then draw, use, and wield items normally. It also reduces its penalty to Strength by 2 and increases its base speed to 30 feet in its solid form. Tierees are not limited to ordinary gear when using incorporation. A creative tieree can incorporate other loose and unattended objects to give it a solid form, such as a pile of leaves, sticks, or enough rubble to cover its body head to toe. The GM has final say if these alternative objects provide any additional bonus (such as DR/bludgeoning when made of rocks), but without feats or other abilities, incorporation generally softens unworked material enough to only provide the benefits listed here.
Inherent Agility: Tierees always treat Acrobatics as a class skill. If Acrobatics is already a class skill for a tieree, it gains a +1 racial bonus on checks with that skill instead.
Fluidic Solid: Without incorporating something onto its body, a tieree can’t grapple, draw, use, or wield items, and it can only carry its light load, lift its medium load, and push or pull its heavy load. Anything heavier than those limits—or which attempts to grapple the tieree—passes through the tieree’s body and becomes coated in its ooze. When a tieree in its natural form collides with a surface or falls far enough that most creatures would take damage, it takes no damage, but instead splatters into a puddle and loses its next turn as its body returns to its normal shape. A tieree in its solid form can choose to splatter, but must then reincorporate everything it was wearing after returning to its natural form. Otherwise, it takes damage normally.
Languages: Tierees begin play speaking Common and Aklo. Tierees with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following languages: Dwarven, Goblin, Orcish, or Undercommon.
Adalisian Tieree Heritage Traits

Adalisian tierees are tieree oozes who absorbed one or more of the relics of Adalis, causing their malleable forms to incorporate the power of those relics into their natural repertoire.

Adalisian tierees gain all of the ancestry traits of other tieree, except as noted here.

Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Dexterity, +2 Charisma, –4 Strength. Adalisian Tierees are as strong and agile as other tierees, but they often fall behind their peers in education so they can focus on their bond to the relics of Adalis.
Form Relic (Sp)

As a full-round action that doesn’t provoke attacks of opportunity, an Adalisian tieree can form one of the three relics of Adalis, treating the relic as an incorporated item for up to 1 minute per character level each day (minimum 3 minutes). These minutes do not need to be used consecutively, but they are used in 1-minute increments. If the tieree already has a relic formed, she can change it into another relic as a standard action that doesn’t reset the duration of the effect.

Relics formed in this way are magical, have no enhancement bonus, and grant Damage Reduction 1 of their appropriate type. An Adalisian tieree with a Charisma score of 13 or higher can cast magic weapon as part of forming her relic (even if she forms the shield) to increase its enhancement bonus by +1 for the duration (which also increases the relic’s granted DR to 2), but each round of her relic’s duration counts as 2 while it is enhanced in this way.

At 5th level, an Adalisian tieree with a Charisma score of 13 or higher can instead cast greater magic weapon as part of forming her relic (even if she forms the shield) to increase its enhancement bonus as described in that spell (which also increases the relic’s granted DR accordingly). In place of increasing her enhancement bonus by +1, the tieree can gain the full benefits of her relic instead.

This replaces coating.

Alternate Ancestry Traits

Attentive Coating: Tierees created from shoggoths can focus their sight in multiple directions at a time. As a move action, a tieree with this trait in its natural form can gain all-around vision for up to 1 round per character level each day. These rounds need not be used consecutively.

This ability alters and replaces coating.

Gelatinous Coating: Tierees created from gelatinous cubes can become transparent when in their natural form. As a standard action, the tieree can become invisible for up to 1 round per character level each day (minimum 3). These rounds need not be used consecutively This otherwise functions as a non-magical vanish spell. The tieree treats its character level as its caster level.

This ability alters and replaces coating.

Ochre Coating: Tierees created from ochre jellies have an acidic touch. As a standard action, they can cover an incorporated weapon with acid, dealing 1d6 additional acid damage when they hit for up to 1 round per character level each day (minimum 3). These rounds need not be used consecutively. This additional damage multiplies on a critical hit based on the incorporated weapon. If the incorporated weapon is already corrosive, it gains the benefits of corrosive burst for the duration instead. Corrosive burst weapons are unaffected by ochre coating.

This ability alters and replaces coating.

Suction Coating: Tierees created from black puddings have a climb speed of 20 feet and the +8 racial bonus on Climb checks that come with it while in their natural form. For 1 round per character level each day (minimum 3), a tieree with suction coating can benefit from a non-magical spider climb effect. These rounds need not be used consecutively.

This ability alters and replaces coating.

Favored Class Bonuses
Any: Add +1 round to the duration of the tieree’s coating per day.
Any (Adalisian): The Adalisian tieree increases the duration of her form relic ability by +1/4 minutes. This option has no effect unless the tieree has selected it four times (or another increment of four).
Alchemist: Gain +1/6 of the Squeezing Form ancestry feat. If you have that feat already, you can instead squeeze through places as if you were up to 1/6 size-categories smaller while under the effects of any mutagen.
Brawler: Add +1/3 acid damage to the brawler’s unarmed strike damage.
Druid: Gain +1/4 use of wild shape per day. If the druid can wild shape at will, this becomes a +1/4 bonus to confirm critical hits while in wild shape (max +5), and it doesn’t stack with Critical Focus.
Monk: Add +1/3 acid damage to the monk’s unarmed strike damage.
Rogue: Choose one—add +1/3 to the DC of poisons the rogue applies to incorporated weapons; or the rogue can incorporate 1/3 of a poison vial and apply doses of that poison to its incorporated weapons as a swift action. The rogue never risks poisoning itself with incorporated poisons.
Sorcerer: Add +1/2 point of acid damage to spells that deal acid damage cast by the sorcerer.
Wizard: Add a +1 bonus on concentration checks made due to taking damage while casting wizard spells.
